title: Compass exposure audit
one_line: Anyone can copy how the Question Compass behaves by asking it questions. This page says what leaks, what to change, and how we will know each change works.

bottom_line.label: Firewall read, 2026-10-17
bottom_line.text: The project's firewall had no custom rules. Only the platform's automatic attack mitigation was active. A log-only rule (10 requests per minute per IP on POST /api/compass) was published on 2026-10-18 at 00:34:58Z. It blocks nothing. A one-time check of what it logged is scheduled for 2026-10-18 at 7 PM. Receipt 2026-10-17--compass-ratelimit-log-publish--ZH.

bottom_line.label: Over-sharing
bottom_line.text: Every answer returns the model's whole output. The screen uses about a third of it. The rest is step-by-step reasoning that a copier would love to have as free training labels.

bottom_line.label: No secrets found
bottom_line.text: The instructions we give the model, the Y-gate thresholds (the cut-offs that grade how sure an answer is) and the scoring math are not in anything a browser can download. Only field names and a few internal labels are.

bottom_line.label: Real defense
bottom_line.text: Hiding fields makes copying more expensive but cannot stop it. What actually limits a copier is how many questions they can ask, and what lets us prove copying afterward is a hidden mark in the answers.

decisions.question: Trim what anonymous visitors get back?
decisions.recommended: Yes. Return only what the screen shows, plus one sealed (encrypted) package so saving later still works.
decisions.why: Saves nothing on cost, removes the most useful labels for a copier.

decisions.question: What should signed-in people get back from the question call?
decisions.recommended: Option A: only the product fields. The full output is read from the owner-only pages the app already uses.
decisions.why: A free account is cheap to make. Option B turns it into unlimited full-detail sampling.

decisions.question: Set the volume limits.
decisions.recommended: The firewall was read on 2026-10-17: no custom rules existed. A log-only rule (10 per minute per IP) is now live. Watch a day of logs, then promote it to the default 429 action. A daily cap cannot be a Vercel rule, because Hobby and Pro windows top out at 10 minutes, so a daily cap needs an app-level counter and a line in /privacy first. Still decide whether to pull ticket GW-002 (gateway limits and spend caps) forward from its 28 October waiver, which is 11 days out.
decisions.why: Today's limit lives in one server's memory, so a spread-out copier is not slowed. The platform rule counts per region, so it is a soft cap, not a global one.

decisions.question: Keep the Observatory code map public?
decisions.recommended: Move it behind the admin login, or drop the risk rows.
decisions.why: It lists file names, sizes and a note that the gate lacks tests. Low risk, but it is the one public map to the gate.

decisions.question: Measure watermark capacity before choosing a scheme?
decisions.recommended: Yes, read-only, on stored receipts, counts only.
decisions.why: The mark only works if answers contain enough wording choices to carry it. We do not know yet that they do.

decisions.question: Send the new no-copying terms to counsel?
decisions.recommended: Yes, with the question of how anonymous visitors accept terms.
decisions.why: Terms today say only: do not scrape or reverse-engineer.

fields.read_by: save only, to recompute the Y-gate
fields.action: move behind auth, carried in the sealed package

leaks.verdict: expected: screens and sample data use the answer shape
low: Observatory ships an internal risk list

leak_notes: Method: fresh npm run build, then a text search of everything a browser can download and of public/. No source maps.
public/ names computeYGate and file sizes in forge-cut.html and observatory/data.arcs-v9.json. Structure only, no thresholds or prompt text.
The CI check leak-check was red on main on 2026-09-27. Not rerun here. Current state unknown.
The earliest-public-disclosure list for patent counsel is a separate chip. This page only notes what is public.

controls.name: Trimmed anonymous answer plus sealed package
controls.plain: Anonymous visitors get only what the screen shows. A sealed (AES-256-GCM encrypted) package carries the rest so saving after sign-in works and cannot be forged.
controls.bad: Today's full answer saved as a fixture: every extra field is flagged
controls.good: Trimmed answer with sealed package passes; saved receipt's Y-gate equals the one from the full answer; a flipped byte or a package over 7 days old is rejected

controls.name: Browser leak check
controls.plain: A script searches the built site for the model instructions and gate constants and fails the build if any appear.
controls.bad: A file containing the prompt sentinel, SATOSHI_MIN_NCI and manifoldCurvature must fail

controls.name: Hidden watermark
controls.plain: About 40 small wording choices in each answer, picked by a secret formula from the question text. Nothing is stored. Run a suspect product on a known question and count matches.
controls.bad: Unmarked or reworded text scores low; 1,000 unrelated texts: none over the line
controls.good: Intact marked answer scores over the line

controls.name: Limits that hold across servers
controls.plain: A Vercel firewall rule on the question call, plus a per-account daily cap and a daily spend breaker. Status: the firewall rule is published in log-only mode; blocking, the daily cap and the spend breaker are not done.
controls.stage: partly done: log-only rule live, nothing blocks yet
controls.bad: 11 requests in 60 seconds spread over 3 servers: today's limiter allows all 11
controls.good: 5 requests in 60 seconds from one visitor all pass

controls.name: Probing detector
controls.plain: Flags the same question tried with many setting combinations, near-identical questions in a row, metronome timing, and never following the suggested follow-ups.
controls.bad: One question across 9 setting combinations, then 50 template variants in 10 minutes: must flag
controls.good: Real session timing, 200 or more sessions: under 1% falsely flagged

controls.name: No-copying terms
controls.plain: Adds a clause against training or distilling a model on outputs. See the text below.
controls.bad: Page without the clause fails a text check
controls.good: Clause present, zero em-dashes, linked from the question box

terms_text: You agree not to use the compass, its outputs, or its responses to build, train, fine-tune, evaluate or distill any machine-learning model or competing product. You agree not to access it by automated means other than through an interface we provide, not to run it at volume to collect outputs, and not to attempt to extract its instructions, scoring rules, or internal structure. Using the compass for your own decisions, and keeping and sharing your own receipts, is always allowed. If we find a breach we may limit or end access without refund, and we will tell you why.

human: Read the five decisions first. Everything else is evidence for them.
If a control has no known-bad test that fails today, do not count it as working. Ask what its test is.
Ask of any hidden-field proposal: what does the screen lose? If the answer is nothing, it is safe to approve.
A watermark is evidence for a lawyer, not a lock. Approve it for proof, not for prevention.
A limit you cannot see in the firewall settings is not a limit. Ask to see the rule.
Anything touching what anonymous visitors store needs a privacy line first.
agent: Do not change production route behavior without an explicit approval recorded against the decision id.
Before building any control, write its known-bad and known-good fixture and confirm bad fails and good passes.
Never mint an ADR or seed number until a decision is approved. Use scripts/oracle.py next at that point.
Never add an anonymous write path. Counters keyed to people need a privacy change first.
Run scripts from the worktree, never by the main checkout path. Merge with gh pr merge --merge and log one decision receipt per merge.
Never degrade answers silently. The response ladder is log, challenge, deny.
After a build, re-run the browser leak search before any merge touching the compass route or public/.

glossary.plain: The ARCS product that takes a decision question and returns a recommended direction.
Copying a model's behavior by asking it many questions and training a cheaper imitation on the answers.
The step that grades how sure an answer is (green, yellow, red and other states) from the answer itself.
A 0 to 100 score the model gives for how confident the answer honestly is. Around 50 means genuinely uncertain.
The open ticket for gateway-level request limits and daily spend caps. Waived until 28 October.
The closed ticket for today's interim limit: 10 requests per minute per address, counted in one server's memory.
The full answer, encrypted so the browser can carry it but not read it. Saving after sign-in decrypts it on the server.
Small wording choices picked by a secret formula, so a copy can be matched back to us. Evidence, not a lock.
A test pair. The bad case must fail the check and the good case must pass, or the check proves nothing.

tables.title: What the firewall looked like on 2026-10-17
tables.intro: Read with the Vercel command line, read-only. The Vercel documentation is the source for the limits.
rows: None. Status read 'Not configured'; no draft changes pending.
Automatic attack mitigation active (the only rule, sys_dos_mitigation). Attack mode off, bot protection off, AI bots allowed, OWASP ruleset off, 0 bypass IPs.
3.5k allowed (peak 2.1k in the first hour, cause not traced), 315 denied by the platform rule, 19 challenged, 0 attacks mitigated. Not broken out by route.
'Compass rate limit (log)': POST /api/compass, 10 per 60 seconds per IP, fixed window, action log (blocks nothing). Published 2026-10-18T00:34:58Z.
Hobby and Pro: 10 seconds to 10 minutes. Only Enterprise reaches 1 hour. So no hourly or daily Vercel rule on these plans. The team's plan was not confirmed.
Hobby: 1 rate-limit rule per project. Pro: 40.
Per region, so traffic spread across regions can exceed the limit.
Not documented. A challenge is built for a browser that can solve it, and the default 429 body is not our JSON message, so the page may show its generic error. Not tested.
Docs describe publishing as applying to the production deployment; no preview-only condition found. Not tested.
